parts.t: Whalley condos are apartment units in strata buildings, most of them in and around Surrey City Centre near the SkyTrain. Every price range shows here, from older low-rise buildings to newer towers, so you can compare them in one place. To learn the neighbourhood first, read my
Whalley guide
Written by
Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®

Most condos in Whalley are within walking distance of a SkyTrain station, and that's often why buyers start here. Before you firm up, I go through the strata's paperwork with you, line by line. I've been a REALTOR® since 2015 with more than $500M in sales, and I'm in the top 1% of Fraser Valley Realtors.

In Paragon, the MLS® system local REALTORS® use, Whalley is a sub-area of North Surrey, and it takes in Surrey City Centre. Below it, you'll find what the City Centre Plan means for condo buyers, how the SkyTrain connects the area, and what to read in the strata records before you buy.

Whalley is in the City of Surrey, so Surrey's bylaws and plans apply. City Centre is its core. The City of Surrey's City Centre Plan describes the area as changing from a suburban town centre into a walkable, transit-oriented downtown for the area south of the Fraser River. Learn more about the plans for the area on my
Surrey land use plans
page.

The City is updating the plan. The update enables more transit-oriented development around the SkyTrain stations, plans for more parks and amenities, and allows more growth in the Bolivar Heights area next door. If you'd like more space and a yard, my
Bolivar Heights homes for sale
page lists homes just north of City Centre.

Three Expo Line stations serve Whalley: Gateway, Surrey Central and King George. Many condo buildings in City Centre are a short walk from one of them, so you can commute without a car. If transit matters to you, start your search with the buildings closest to a station.

The Province is also building the Surrey Langley SkyTrain. It extends the Expo Line from King George Station along Fraser Highway to Langley City. For condo owners in Whalley, that means the same line will reach further east into Surrey and Langley.

blocks.text: What you own when you buy a condo

parts.t: When you buy a Whalley condo, you're buying a strata lot: your unit, plus a share of everything else in the building. The roof, lobby, elevators, parkade and gardens are common property, owned together by all the owners through the strata corporation. An elected council handles the budget, sets the monthly fees and enforces the bylaws. In a tower, your balcony and parking stall may be limited common property, meaning they're for your use only. The strata plan shows what's assigned to your unit.

The Form B: Information Certificate is the strata's official snapshot of a unit and the building. A buyer, an owner or someone they authorize can request it, and the strata has 7 days to provide it. Look for the monthly fee, any money the seller still owes, special levies already approved, and the contingency reserve fund balance. Attached you should find the budget, the rules and, if there is one, the latest depreciation report.

A strata with five or more lots has to get a depreciation report every five years in BC. It's a 30-year forecast of what the building's parts will cost to repair or replace. In a newer City Centre tower, check what it says about elevators, mechanical systems and the parkade, then compare it with the reserve fund balance on the Form B.

blocks.text: Before you buy a Whalley condo

parts.t: Request the Form B and go through every page that comes with it.
Read the bylaws and rules, plus two years of council and AGM minutes.
Match your unit, parking stall and locker to the strata plan.
Check the pet bylaws, since MLS listings don't show them.
Time the walk to Gateway, Surrey Central or King George.

blocks.text: Is Surrey City Centre in Whalley?

parts.t: Yes. In Paragon, City Centre sits inside the Whalley sub-area of North Surrey, around the Gateway, Surrey Central and King George SkyTrain stations.

blocks.text: Which SkyTrain stations serve Whalley condos?

parts.t: Three Expo Line stations serve Whalley: Gateway, Surrey Central and King George. Many condo buildings are a short walk from one of them.

blocks.text: How will the Surrey Langley SkyTrain affect Whalley?

parts.t: The Province is extending the Expo Line from King George Station along Fraser Highway to Langley City, so Whalley riders will be able to stay on the train heading east.

blocks.text: What do I own when I buy a Whalley condo?

parts.t: Your strata lot, plus a shared interest in the building's common property through the strata corporation.

blocks.text: What should I look for in the Form B?

parts.t: The strata fee, money owed by the seller, approved special levies and the contingency reserve fund balance, plus the attached budget, rules and depreciation report.

blocks.text: How often does a condo building get a depreciation report?

parts.t: Every five years, for stratas with five or more lots. It's usually attached to the Form B.
